- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The 1922 Peace dollar was minted from 1921 to 1935 and again in 1965, designed by Anthony de Francisci to commemorate the end of World War I.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The 1922 Peace dollar features Lady Liberty on the obverse and an eagle at rest on the reverse.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Over 51 million 1922 Peace dollars were minted in Philadelphia.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The value of the 1922 Peace dollar can range from $15-$500 or more, depending on its condition.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The user’s 1893 Morgan dollar has a low mintage of 378,000 coins, making it a scarce date in the series.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The value estimates for the 1893 Morgan dollar range from $20-$1,500 or more, depending on its condition.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] A near-mint 1893 Morgan dollar can fetch a premium price, with specific estimates of $400-$1,200 or more.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Both the Morgan and Peace dollars contain 90% silver and 10% copper, weighing 26.73 grams each.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The silver content of each coin is approximately 0.7734 troy oz of silver.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The melt value of the coins is influenced by the current price of silver, which is around $18-20 per troy ounce as of the conversation.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Error coins are coins minted with mistakes or irregularities, which can significantly increase their value.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Types of error coins include misprinted dates, misaligned dies, double strikes, off-center strikes, wrong metal, and mule coins.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The value of error coins depends on rarity, condition, demand, and authenticity.
